# Portenv: full description for language models

> Portenv — your product, built by a team of AI agents (Portenv is short for portable environment; also heard as 'port env'). Each agent gets a role, its own user account and its own copy of your code, inside a workspace sealed off from your Mac. They build, review and hand work to each other. Anything that matters waits for your yes.

Status: in development. The Mac app is not available to download yet. This text describes what Portenv is being built to do; the short links below say "coming soon" until each part exists.

## Teams

- You pick a ready-made team of agents with one command (choosing it in the app comes next): Starter (a lead, a builder and a reviewer), App product team (engineering, product design, trust and safety, release and DevOps) or Orchestrate (a coordinator, an independent reviewer and parallel builders).
- You read exactly what each agent is told before you approve it; an agent's model is set by editing its settings.
- Each agent is its own user with its own copy of the code and only the access its job needs. Agents can't push, and they never get your encryption keys.
- Decisions land in Needs you; Team activity shows who asked whom for what, in order.

## Boxes

- Each project gets a box: a workspace with its files, history, tools and settings together.
- A box runs on your Mac or on a server you own. Move To takes it from one to another and picks up exactly where you left off.
- A box saves as you go and works offline; saves go out when the network is back.
- You can make a save point before a risky change, and revert to it later. Reverting never throws away the work it replaces.

## Security

- Each box is encrypted on your device before it is saved, with keys kept in your Mac's Keychain.
- Only one machine has a box open at a time, so two copies never drift apart.
- Agents work inside a box but can never read its encryption keys or passwords.
- Portenv opens no public or inbound ports on your machines.

## Agents

- You invite an agent to one box. It can continue your work in your own sessions, or, later, work in a lane of its own.
- You see what each agent does, by name. You can revoke it at any time, and its access ends at once.
- When an agent connects, Portenv makes a save point, so you can undo everything it did.

Ways in, in the order they are being built:

1. SSH and the `portenv` command-line tool, with a published skill, for a box on your own server.
2. Webhooks: your agent is told when a box needs it, for example when a tool is waiting for an answer.
3. MCP on the agent's computer (stdio).
4. Remote MCP on your own server.
5. A web terminal on your own server, for agents that only have a browser.

## The command-line tool

- The command is `portenv`. Every action in the app is also a command, and every command can answer in JSON.
- When something fails, the message says what happened and what to do next.
- Install it from https://portenv.com/cli once it is released. The packages `@portenv/cli` on npm and `portenv-cli` on PyPI are placeholders for now and install nothing.

## Short links

- https://portenv.com/cli: install the command-line tool (coming soon)
- https://portenv.com/skill: the skill for agents (coming soon)
- https://portenv.com/mcp: connect over MCP (coming soon)

## Open source

The Mac app, the runner, the in-box agent and the save format are Apache-2.0, in one public repository at https://github.com/portenv/portenv. Portenv works with your own servers and storage, without a Portenv account.
